label: Figure 17.4: Open market operations
alt: Loanable funds market: a downward-sloping demand curve D and two vertical supply curves, S1 on the left and S2 on the right. Arrows show buying securities moving supply from S1 to S2 and selling securities moving it back.
caption: When the central bank buys government securities, banks’ funds rise and the supply of loanable funds shifts right from S1 to S2, lowering the interest rate from i1 to i2 (expansionary). When it sells securities, supply shifts back left from S2 to S1 and the interest rate rises from i2 to i1 (contractionary).
